metadata.title: Lingo Agent
metadata.description: An open-source AI English assistant that remembers you.

home.badge: Open source · Self-hostable · Bring your own models
home.title: Your AI English assistant
home.subtitle: It remembers what you know and what you keep getting wrong.
home.note: Works from A1 to C2. Explanations can lean on Chinese or stay all in English.

weekend.user: Last weekend I go hiking with my sister and it was amazing.
weekend.reply: Sounds like a great weekend! One small fix: I went hiking — “last weekend” needs the past tense.
weekend.note: You often use the present tense for past events, so this week's practice has a few more of these.

memory.name: reflect_memory
memory.detail: Saved: often goes hiking with their sister at weekends

word.user: What does “reluctant” mean? I saw it in a news article about remote work.
word.reply: Reluctant means not wanting to do something: “Many workers are reluctant to go back to the office.”
word.note: It's on your word list now, so you'll see it again in a review in a few days.
word.summary: read 1 memory · added 1 word · no grammar errors

goal.user: I want to take the IELTS next year, but my vocabulary is too small.
goal.memory: Read: you're around B1 and have 20 minutes a day
goal.reply: A year is plenty of time. Let's grow your vocabulary steadily — I'd suggest the IELTS word book with 15 new words a day.

tool.name: propose_word_book
tool.card: Switch to IELTS · 15 new words a day

goal.note: Nothing changes until you confirm, and you can undo it afterwards.

memory.name: reflect_memory
memory.detail: Saved: aims to take the IELTS next year

goal.summary: read 3 memories · updated 1 · proposed a word book

memoryStill.memory: You enjoy the outdoors and often hike at weekends

memory.title: An assistant that remembers you
memory.body: Your goals, interests and usual mistakes. Each chat picks up where you left off, so you never have to introduce yourself again.

grammar.title: Grammar tracking and mastery
grammar.body: Every grammar point has a mastery level and the evidence behind it: which sentence went wrong, which time you got it right.

vocab.title: FSRS vocabulary
vocab.body: Oxford 3000, CET-4/6, IELTS and more, reviewed on an FSRS spaced-repetition schedule. New words from your chats can go in too.

placement.title: Placement test
placement.body: About 10 minutes for a CEFR level and an estimated vocabulary size. The assistant pitches its explanations at your level.

transparency.title: See everything the AI does
transparency.body: Every button that calls a model is marked AI; open it to see which model and roughly how many tokens. What the assistant read and saved unfolds under each reply.

models.title: Your models, self-hosted
models.body: Connect DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Qwen, SiliconFlow and more. Runs on a small server, and your data stays with you.

trust.eyebrow: Transparency is the core of this product
trust.title: Everything the assistant remembers, you can see, edit and delete
trust.body: When the assistant wants to switch your word book or set a goal, it asks first. Nothing changes until you confirm, and you can undo it afterwards.
trust.cardTitle: Switch your word book to IELTS?
trust.cardBody: You mentioned taking IELTS next year. Nothing changes until you confirm.
trust.hint: ← Open the AI mark: which models it calls and roughly how many tokens

login.title: Log in
login.description: Welcome back. Pick up where you left off.

register.title: Create an account
register.description: Start practicing English with your AI assistant.

diagnosis.never: When you keep making mistakes on the same grammar point, your assistant looks for the cause: once a week, and after a practice set.

diagnosis.off: Assistant's diagnosis is off. You can turn it on in <link>Settings</link>.

grammar.title: Grammar mastery
grammar.description: Worked out from your mistakes and correct uses in conversation: {mastered}% or more counts as mastered, below {weak}% as weak. Open one to see why; if a tag is wrong, delete it and the mastery is recomputed.
grammar.empty: Nothing yet. Write a few sentences in English in a conversation and the assistant will note the grammar you get wrong and right here.

kc.counts: {mistakes} mistakes · used correctly {produced} times in your own words · {recognized} right answers in tests

skills.title: Skill estimates
skills.description: From the placement test: a level for grammar, an estimated size for vocabulary. All on one A1–C2 scale.
skills.emptyHint: After the placement test, each skill's level shows up here.

clear.title: Delete all learning records
clear.description: Deletes all grammar evidence, mastery and skill estimates, the grammar tags in what the assistant did under replies, and the assistant's diagnoses with the memory they wrote. Other memories and conversations stay.
clear.confirm: Delete all learning records? This cannot be undone.

shadowing.title: Shadowing
shadowing.description: Sentences you read aloud and how they went, newest first. Recordings aren't kept. Deleting a reading doesn't undo what it already counted toward speaking or word pronunciation.
shadowing.empty: No readings yet. Tap the microphone by an assistant reply, a reading paragraph or a review example to start.
shadowing.clearConfirm: Delete all your readings? What they counted toward speaking and word pronunciation stays.

connections.title: Model connections
connections.description: Add the model providers you want to use. Keys are encrypted on the server and never shown again.
connections.none: No connections yet. Add one below to start chatting.
connections.name: Name
connections.apiKeyHint: Leave empty only for local servers that need no key (e.g. Ollama).
connections.asrNotSupported: This connection does not support speech-to-text (its server has no /audio/transcriptions endpoint). Use a speech-to-text provider such as SiliconFlow, Groq, OpenAI or local Speaches.
connections.visionNotSupported: This model does not accept images (the server refused a request with an image). Pick a model with image input for vision.
connections.confirmDelete: Delete the connection "{name}"? Routes using it will skip it.
connections.defaultModelHint: Chat uses it when no model is set for it. For a connection used only for speech-to-text or images, enter that model and pick the matching test.
connections.modelPlaceholder: Pick from the list or type a model name
connections.modelsFound: The key works: {count} chat models available.
connections.modelsFoundNone: The key works, but no chat models were listed. Type a model name.
connections.modelsFailed: Couldn't fetch the model list: {error}. You can still type a model name.
connections.modelsNoMatch: No matching model. Your text will be used as-is.
connections.noDefaultModel: No default model yet: this connection isn't used for chat until you save one.
connections.newKeyPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current key
connections.renamePresetHint: The server's default routes find this provider by its name. After renaming, chat uses this connection's default model instead (your own routes are updated automatically).
connections.offHint: Off: no feature uses this connection. Its settings and key are kept; turn it back on any time.
connections.ttsNotSupported: This connection can't read aloud (the server has no /audio/speech endpoint, or no such voice). Use a read-aloud model from Azure Speech, SiliconFlow, OpenAI or a local Speaches instead.
connections.testVoiceHint: This connection only reads aloud and assesses pronunciation. Pick a voice to test reading aloud, or pronunciation to test assessment; which voices are used, and whether it assesses pronunciation, is set in the Read aloud and Pronunciation routes below.
connections.testRealtimeHint: This connection only takes realtime voice calls (Gemini Live). Pick a Live model to test; the test only opens a session and uses no audio. Which model calls use is set in the Realtime voice route below.
connections.azureRegionHint: The region of your Speech resource, such as eastasia, eastus or chinaeast2. The address follows from it.

source.default: Using the default order from the server configuration.
source.auto: Automatic: each connection's default model, in the order the connections were added.

route.editHint: Pick a connection and a model for each row. The first one is used; the rest take over if it fails.
route.modelsFailed: Couldn't fetch the model list. Type a model name.
route.modelsNoMatch: No matching model. Your text will be used as-is.

chat.title: Chat model
chat.description: Models are tried in order; if one fails, the next one takes over.
chat.none: No chat model is usable yet. Add a connection and save its default model.

reflect.title: Background memory model
reflect.description: Runs after each reply: decides what the assistant should remember about you and writes conversation summaries. A smaller, cheaper model is fine here.
reflect.none: No model available: the assistant won't remember anything new until you add a chat model.

vision.title: Image model (vision)
vision.description: Reads images and scanned PDF pages, and answers messages that carry images. Pick models that can see images: chat models are not used for this automatically.
vision.none: Not set up: images and scanned PDFs can't be read until you add a model here.

exercise_generate.title: Exercise writer
exercise_generate.description: Writes practice items and the quiz cards in chat. Items are written in one structured pass: a fast model without reasoning (or reasoning set to off) makes quizzes much quicker.
exercise_generate.none: No model available: exercises can't be written until a chat model is added.

exercise_critic.title: Exercise reviewer
exercise_critic.description: Solves each new item before checking it and sends faulty ones back to be rewritten. A model from another vendor than the writer's catches more mistakes.
exercise_critic.none: No model available: exercises can't be written until a chat model is added.

asr.title: Speech-to-text
asr.description: Transcribes voice messages and audio files (an OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions API, e.g. Groq, OpenAI, SiliconFlow or a local speaches server).
asr.none: Not set up: voice messages can't be transcribed until you add a model here.

tts.title: Read aloud
tts.description: Reads assistant replies, words and examples with a server voice (Azure Speech, or an OpenAI-compatible /audio/speech endpoint such as SiliconFlow, OpenAI or a local speaches). Sentences already read are cached.
tts.none: Not set up: learners' browsers read aloud.

words.title: Word pronunciations
words.description: The read-aloud models that make a word book's pronunciations ahead of time (Settings → Word pronunciations). A slow voice is fine here, e.g. Bailian qwen-audio. When none of them can be used, words are made like everything else read aloud. A learner reading a word gets these recordings first.
words.none: Not set up: word pronunciations use the read-aloud route.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation
pronunciation.description: Scores learners' pronunciation when they read after the model: overall, per word and per sound (Azure Speech only for now, model pronunciation). Without it, shadowing compares a transcript with the sentence and gives only a rough result.
pronunciation.none: Not set up: shadowing compares a transcript instead (no shadowing without speech-to-text either).

realtime.title: Realtime voice
realtime.description: Learners talk to the assistant on a call: one model listens and speaks directly, and can be interrupted (realtime APIs of OpenAI, Qwen-Omni and StepFun). The next one in order is tried only when connecting; a call never switches midway. It costs much more than speaking practice; set its limits under “Realtime voice limits” below.
realtime.none: Not set up: no realtime calls; speaking practice still uses transcription and read-aloud.

route.allOff: Every model here is switched off. Turn one on to use this.
route.switchedOff: {ref} is off and will be skipped.
route.voiceNone: No built-in voice: the next model or the browser reads this language
route.voicesHint: Under each model you can choose a voice per language; empty uses the built-in one. An Azure connection offers its voices; for a qwen-audio model, describe the voice in English (e.g. "A calm British man").
route.providedBy: Provided by {name}: you don't have a model of your own for this.
route.quotaExhausted: Your quota from {name} for this is used up for now. Add a connection of your own, or wait for it to reset (UTC).
route.reasoningHint: Reasoning models think before they answer: the more they think, the later the first word appears. Default sends nothing. Bailian and SiliconFlow only switch it on or off (low, medium and high all mean on); Anthropic's and DeepSeek's own APIs are unaffected. If a model doesn't support it, its calls fail: set it back to Default.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Model calls by this account, and by members on your connections, per UTC day. No prices are built in: enter yours to see estimated costs.
usage.empty: No model calls in this period.
usage.costPartial: Partial: some models have no price for what they used
usage.costFootnote: * Some usage has no price and is left out. Costs are estimates at current prices, not a bill.

prices.title: Prices
prices.hint: Enter your provider's prices; leave a box empty to not count it. Lists models used in this range and ones already priced.
prices.noModels: No models used in this range.

display.title: Display
display.showActivity: Show what the assistant did under its replies
display.showActivityHint: Memories read and saved, grammar mistakes marked. Hiding it changes the display only: everything is still recorded, and the Memory page still shows it all.

background.title: Background work
background.description: The assistant prepares some things while you are away. Each can be switched off; it is then done when you need it, with a short wait.
background.budgetExhausted: Today's background budget is used up; it resets tomorrow (UTC). What you start yourself still works.
background.budgetOff: An admin switched off all background model calls. What you start yourself still works.

practice_prefetch.name: Prepare the next practice set
practice_prefetch.hint: After you finish a grammar set, the next one is generated in the background so it opens without a wait.

article_prerewrite.name: Rewrite new articles ahead
article_prerewrite.hint: When the feeds you follow have new articles, they are rewritten for your level with comprehension questions in the background, so they open without a wait.

word_examples_prefetch.name: Write AI example sentences ahead
word_examples_prefetch.hint: For words you will review or learn in the next day that have no real example sentence, AI sentences are written in the background, so the card shows them when you turn it over.

diagnosis.name: The assistant's diagnosis
diagnosis.hint: For grammar points you keep getting wrong, the assistant looks for likely root causes in the background, across their prerequisites and the points they are often confused with, quoting your own sentences, and practice brings the related points up more often. Weekly, and after a practice set with many new mistakes.

background.budgetHint: How many tokens background calls (ones no learner is waiting for) may use per day, from midnight UTC. Checked before each piece of background work starts, so the last one may go slightly over. 0 switches all background calls off. Chat, grading and other things learners start are never limited.

skip.budget_exhausted: Today's background budget was used up.

jobs.article_prerewrite: Rewrite new articles for readers' levels
jobs.word_examples_prefetch: Write AI example sentences for the coming day's words
jobs.diagnosis: The assistant's diagnosis (at most weekly per learner)
jobs.tts_cache_cleanup: Clear read-aloud audio unused for 30 days

wordAudio.title: Word pronunciations
wordAudio.description: Generate a word book's pronunciations ahead of time with the first model in the read-aloud route above. Learners reading a word aloud in the word bubble or on a review card get it straight away, with no model call. Only admins see this section.
wordAudio.unavailable: No read-aloud model reads English yet. Set one up under Read aloud above first.
wordAudio.progress: {done} of {total} done{failed, plural, =0 {} one {, # failed} other {, # failed}}
wordAudio.retryHint: Failed words were not generated. Generate this book again to fill in just those.
wordAudio.cancelQuestion: What was generated is kept; the rest won't be.
wordAudio.deleteBookQuestion: Delete this book's pronunciations? Words other books share go too.
wordAudio.deleted: Deleted {count, plural, one {# pronunciation} other {# pronunciations}}.
wordAudio.priceHint: Check the vendor's pricing page; the price is only used for the estimate, and without one only characters are shown. Azure's free tier allows 500,000 characters a month and 20 requests a minute; past the limit it waits and tries again.
wordAudio.estimate: {words} words, {pieces} pieces of audio, {existing} already there, {toMake} to generate.
wordAudio.slowModel: This model takes about {seconds} s a word, one word at a time, so it's slower than the requests per minute suggest.
wordAudio.missing: No voice for {accents}; it won't be generated.
wordAudio.storage: {count} word pronunciations, {megabytes} MB. They don't count toward the read-aloud cache's 200 MB or its 30-day cleanup.
wordAudio.old: {count} of them ({megabytes} MB) are in a voice no longer used.
wordAudio.deleteOldQuestion: Delete the pronunciations made before the voice changed?

realtime.title: Realtime voice limits
realtime.description: Realtime calls are billed by the minute for the whole call, so they cost far more than the step-by-step speaking practice. Set how long one call may last and how many minutes each learner gets per day.
realtime.hint: 0 in either box turns realtime calls off. The day starts at 00:00 UTC. With under a minute left today, no call starts; the learner is warned a minute before the end, and at the end the assistant says goodbye and hangs up.
realtime.off: Realtime calls are off for everyone in this workspace.
realtime.usedToday: You have used {used} of {limit} minutes today (UTC).

org.capsHint: Leave a box empty for no cap; 0 turns the capability off. Days and months are UTC.

members.title: Members
members.description: People who use your model connections within the quotas you give them. They never see your keys; you see only how much they use, not what they learn.
members.empty: No members yet. Create an invite link and send it to them.
members.past: {count, plural, one {# past member} other {# past members}}
members.removeQuestion: Remove {name}? They stop using your models right away.

invite.title: Invite
invite.createdHint: Send this link. It's shown only now: copy it before leaving the page.
invite.revokeQuestion: Revoke this invite? The link stops working.

defaults.title: Quotas for new members
defaults.hint: What a member gets when they join. Changing this doesn't change existing members.

membership.title: Main account
membership.description: Another account can lend you its models within a quota. Your own connections always come first.
membership.ownFirst: Whatever you've set up yourself is used first and doesn't count against this quota.

join.title: Join a main account
join.description: Use another account's models within the quota it gives you.
join.privacy: They'll see how much you use, not your conversations, memories or learning records. Your own connections stay first. You can leave any time.

placement.title: Placement test
placement.description: About 10 minutes to find your level; your assistant adjusts explanations and practice to it.

intro.vocab: One English word at a time; say whether you know it. Some are made up, so if you don't know a word, answer "No" rather than guess.
intro.grammar: A sentence with one blank; pick the right one of four options.

aiBadge.label: Uses AI: what it does and roughly how many tokens

feature.chat_message: Your assistant's reply is written by an AI model. After it, the assistant reviews the turn in the background to update your memories, mistakes and words. A longer message (60+ English words) is first checked by an AI model to see whether it is your own writing; if so, the writing coach reviews it sentence by sentence.
feature.chat_image: An AI model reads each image first, so the assistant can talk about it. The reply to that message also comes from the image-reading model.
feature.chat_pdf: PDFs with a text layer are read without AI. Scanned pages are read by an AI model, one call per page.
feature.chat_audio: Your recording is turned into text by a speech-to-text model.
feature.practice_start: The assistant opens the practice with a first message written by an AI model.
feature.plan_start: The assistant opens the planning conversation with a first message written by an AI model, from your test result and learning data. After that, each reply is like any chat message.
feature.lesson_start: When you open a lesson, the assistant speaks first with an AI model: a small question to bring back what you know, the core rule, then a question or two to check you followed (see quiz cards). Each turn after is like a normal chat, with the lesson's material: its state, what it builds on, your recent mistakes and quiz results.
feature.pet_daily_opening: The first time you open the cat each day, the assistant writes the first message of today's conversation with an AI model: a short look back at your last 7 days (numbers counted by code) and one or two suggestions for today. Once a day; it happens while the cat wears the ✦ hair clip. After that, each reply is like any chat message.
feature.practice_set: An AI model writes a set of items on your weak grammar points; another model solves and reviews each one first, and items that fail are rewritten. Bank items fill any gaps. After you finish a set, the next one is written in the background.
feature.practice_grade: Open answers (rewrites, translations, fixing your own sentence) and fixes not in an item's answer list are graded by an AI model: it judges the tested grammar point, explains, and points out other grammar mistakes in your answer. Multiple choice and fill-in answers are graded by code, without AI. Only your first answer to each item is graded.
feature.quiz_card: An AI model writes a set of quiz questions on this grammar point, and another model answers each one first to check it; questions that fail are rewritten. Gaps in a pass quiz are filled from the question bank; understanding checks don't use it. Open answers and explanations in your own words are graded by AI, once per question; choice questions are graded by code. Understanding checks only see whether you got the idea and don't count towards mastery.
feature.memory_edit: Adding or editing a memory turns it into a vector with an embedding model, so the assistant can find it later.
feature.word_examples: An AI model writes two example sentences for this word at your level. They are saved, so the next time anyone asks for this word at this level, no model is called.
feature.message_translate: An AI model translates this message. The translation is saved, so switching back and forth makes no more calls.
feature.workspace_translate: An AI model translates the text in the workspace, paragraph by paragraph as you scroll to it, or one paragraph you ask for in the original. Translations are saved: switching back and forth or opening it again makes no call.
feature.workspace_analyze: An AI model breaks the sentence down: its main clause, the other clauses and what they do, tricky phrases, and what it means in Chinese. The analysis is saved: tapping the same sentence again makes no call.
feature.writing_submit: An AI model reviews your writing sentence by sentence: it finds and explains grammar mistakes, scores four aspects, writes overall feedback and puts unknown words on your word list. Mistakes go into your learner model; scores are only shown.
feature.reading_rewrite: An AI model rewrites this article for your level and writes a few comprehension questions; another model answers each question itself to check it, and a question that fails is rewritten once, then dropped. The rewrite is saved: opening it again at the same level calls no model.
feature.reading_coach: The reading coach answers your questions about this article: each message sends the article (the version for your level, or the beginning of the original) with the conversation, so a reply reads more than a chat turn. Afterwards, as in any chat, memory and grammar notes are updated in the background.
feature.reading_prerewrite: In the background every two hours: new articles of the feeds you follow are rewritten for your level with questions, by the same AI calls as opening an article, within the tenant's daily background budget.
feature.word_examples_prefetch: In the background every six hours: for the words you will review or learn in the next day that have no real example sentence, the same AI call as the "AI examples" button writes two sentences at your level, at most 30 words a time, within the tenant's daily background budget. Learners at the same level share them.
feature.diagnosis: In the background at most weekly (also after a practice set with many new mistakes, at most daily): the AI model reads up to 3 grammar points you keep getting wrong, their prerequisites and the points they are often confused with, and your latest mistakes, and suggests root causes. Conclusions that cannot quote your own sentences are dropped. Within the tenant's daily background budget.
feature.read_aloud: Replies, words and examples are read by the server's read-aloud model; sentences already read are cached and not billed again. You can turn it off in the read-aloud settings and use only this device's voices.
feature.word_audio_prefetch: Started by hand in the settings for one word book: the first model in the read-aloud route reads each word in American and/or British English once and the audio is kept, so learners reading a word aloud play it with no model call. Billed by characters, estimated before it starts; not against the daily background budget.
feature.shadowing: Your recording is scored by a pronunciation assessment model: overall, per word and per sound. The recording is discarded once scored; only the scores are kept. They update your speaking ability, and words you don't say right are marked in your reviews. If assessment fails, a transcript is compared instead.
feature.shadowing_rough: Your recording is transcribed by a speech-to-text model and compared with the sentence word by word, marking words left out, heard as another word, or added. It's a rough result, not a pronunciation score, and isn't counted in your learning record. The recording is discarded once transcribed.
feature.speaking_start: When you start speaking practice, the assistant says the first line of the scene, written by an AI model.
feature.speaking_turn: What you say is transcribed by a speech-to-text model, then an AI model replies in the scene (briefly, read aloud to you). Afterwards, as in any chat, the turn is reviewed in the background to update your memory and grammar notes; very short spoken turns record no mistakes, so a transcription error isn't counted as yours.
feature.speaking_summary: When you finish, an AI model reads the conversation and writes what went well, mistakes with corrections, more natural ways to say things and expressions to try next time, and rates how easy you were to understand. Items that don't quote your own words are dropped; the rating updates your speaking ability.
feature.realtime_call: A live call with the assistant: one model hears you and answers in speech, and you can interrupt it. Usage goes by call length: both voices are counted as audio tokens, and each answer reads the call so far again. Audio tokens cost far more than text, so a minute here costs several times a minute of speaking practice (transcription plus a text reply); that's why calls have per-call and per-day minute limits.

outfits.classic: Scholar: glasses, bow tie, sweater vest

looks.petHint: Keeps you company in a corner of the page; tap it to ask your assistant. The same on every device.
looks.nudgesHint: The pet says in a bubble when words are due, what's left of today's plan, or that a model needs setting up. At most 3 a day; no model calls.
looks.dailyOpening: Sum up on the first open of the day
looks.dailyOpeningHint: The first time you open the desk pet each day, the assistant uses AI to look back at your last 7 days and suggest one or two things for today (a few tokens). The cat wears a ✦ hair clip until then.
looks.workspaceAutoOpenHint: When you paste a whole English text or start writing something longer, the assistant opens the workspace on the right. You can also just tell it to close it, or to stop opening it by itself.
looks.quizProactive: Let the assistant quiz you by itself
looks.quizProactiveHint: After explaining a rule, or when you keep making the same mistake, the assistant may give you a short check card (one or two questions, a few tokens to write; it does not change your mastery). At most once per grammar point in a chat. Off: quiz cards only when you ask for them.
looks.animateHint: Off: a still picture. Also still when your system asks for reduced motion.
